image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet peeks out from behind a half-open timber door in a dim 1840s hallway, one eye visible, a guilty look on his face.

storyboard.claim: Tom protects himself by hiding from the moral problem rather than facing it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom peeking from behind a door, half hidden.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the courtroom-of-conscience thread from the previous explanation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The image shows the act of hiding, which the words describe abstractly.

image.subject: A tin bucket tipped over on a dusty board sidewalk of a small Missouri river town in summer, a whitewashed picket fence beside it with one broken board, heat-shimmer in the air.

storyboard.claim: Opting out of responsibility causes damage that spreads to others.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abandoned tin bucket and broken fence on a dusty street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the hiding idea into a visible consequence.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fallen bucket and broken fence show what is left behind when someone steps away.

image.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard and bloodshot eyes, wearing a torn grey shirt and stained trousers, chained at the wrist, sitting alone on a plank cot in a small stone jail cell.

storyboard.claim: The most vulnerable person in the room pays for others' silence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Muff Potter chained on a cot in a cell.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the person who pays the price.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chain at his wrist shows he is held, not free.

storyboard.claim: Someone else, usually the most vulnerable, ends up paying the price.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Quotation card on plain background.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the general rule after the example of the jail.
storyboard.addedInformation: A general principle worth reading slowly.

image.subject: A knot of respectable townspeople in dark 1840s coats and bonnets stand on a board sidewalk in St. Petersburg, Missouri, heads turned toward a small stone jail at the end of the street.

storyboard.claim: The respectable citizens prefer an easy scapegoat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Townspeople looking toward the jail.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the principle to the town that applies it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The crowd's gaze points at the jail, which shows whom they blame.

image.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in his thirties in a torn, dirty brown coat and slouch hat, a hard face with a scar and an unshaven jaw, walking along a dusty town street with his hands in his coat pockets, not looking at anyone.

storyboard.claim: The lethal predator walks freely among the town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Injun Joe walking a town street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the true threat the town ignores.
storyboard.addedInformation: He moves openly through the street, which shows his freedom.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat with a neutral, thoughtful expression stands among a small crowd of townspeople on a courthouse step, nodding along to what the others are saying.

storyboard.claim: The community agrees on Muff's guilt because it is psychologically convenient.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grey-coated townsman nodding in a crowd.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the townspeople agreeing with the scapegoat story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Everyman stands for the ordinary citizen who goes along.

image.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard and bloodshot eyes, wearing a torn grey shirt and chained at the wrist, grips the bars of a jail window and looks out with a grateful, teary expression.

storyboard.claim: Muff pours out gratitude for the boys' small kindness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Muff gripping jail bars, grateful.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the man whose gratitude the boys receive.
storyboard.addedInformation: His grip on the bars shows how much the gift matters to him.

storyboard.claim: Muff thanks the boys for memories of kindness they repay with silence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-item list of what Muff recalls.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists what the boys once gave him.
storyboard.addedInformation: The list is the favour Muff remembers, which makes the silence worse.

storyboard.claim: Loyalty becomes complicity when it holds a man in chains.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Question card, text only.
storyboard.onScreenText: Is loyalty still loyalty when it keeps a man in chains?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns Muff's thanks into a real question.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question asks the viewer to judge the boys' silence.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet stands outside a small stone jail window, looking in at a chained man, his grin gone.

storyboard.claim: Tom visits the jail and cannot bring himself to speak.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom outside the jail window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts Tom at the scene of his silence.
storyboard.addedInformation: He stands outside the bars, which shows he is free while Muff is not.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt sits on a whitewashed picket fence with his back to a jail, head bowed, hands clasped between his knees, a dusty street in summer light.

storyboard.claim: Tom turns away from the truth he knows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom sitting on a fence with his back turned.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows Tom's choice to look away.
storyboard.addedInformation: His bowed head and turned back show the choice to stay silent.

image.subject: A heavy timber jail door in a small stone building, an iron chain and padlock hanging across it in the afternoon light, a dusty street in front.

storyboard.claim: The town prepares to execute an innocent man in chains.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A chained jail door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the jail that holds the innocent man.
storyboard.addedInformation: The padlock and chain make the wait visible.

image.subject: A quiet middle-aged man with a dark moustache in a dark suit and waistcoat leans on a writing desk with an open book, a half-smile, a lamp on the desk, looking up as if reflecting.

storyboard.claim: It is easy to judge Tom from a safe modern seat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator at a desk with an open book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the narrator in to step back from the judgment.
storyboard.addedInformation: The narrator's safe, seated pose matches the distance the claim describes.

image.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in his thirties in a torn, dirty brown coat and slouch hat stands in the shadow of a courthouse porch, a hard face with a scar, his cold, unblinking stare aimed at the viewer.

storyboard.claim: A boy believes the lethal man will kill him if he speaks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Injun Joe in a porch shadow, staring.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the threat that makes Tom afraid.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cold stare shows why a boy would fear him.

image.subject: A lone man in a slouch hat walks a dusty town street at dusk past whitewashed picket fences, his shadow long in the low sun, the houses shut tight.

storyboard.claim: The killer walks free through town, and a boy fears what he might do.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lone figure on a dusk street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the threat moving through town.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shut houses and long shadow show the town's unease.

image.subject: Two boys, one a freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old in a faded blue shirt and the other a thin, barefoot 13-year-old in ragged homespun clothes with a battered straw hat, clasp hands under a willow tree by a muddy river bank at dusk.

storyboard.claim: Tom's silence is a clash between a childhood oath and a developing conscience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom and Huck clasping hands under a willow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the oath that binds Tom.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clasped hands show the childhood vow as a physical bond.

image.subject: A dim graveyard at midnight with leaning wooden markers, a dead elm tree silhouetted against moonlight through leaves, lit only by a single lantern on the ground.

storyboard.claim: Tom's dreams are infested with the horrors of the graveyard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A midnight graveyard with a lantern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the oath to the memory that haunts Tom.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dead elm and leaning markers recall the murder scene.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt sits up in a narrow bed in a dark bedroom, a single tallow candle on a small table beside him, his face pale and drawn, staring into the dark.

storyboard.claim: Tom is physically deteriorating from the secret.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom sitting up in bed by a candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the cost of the secret on Tom's body.
storyboard.addedInformation: The candle and wakeful pose show sleepless nights.

storyboard.claim: The town has agreed on a false narrative built on Injun Joe's lie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement.
storyboard.onScreenText: A false story, agreed by the whole town.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the trap that Tom is caught in.
storyboard.addedInformation: The town agreed to it, which is the point.

image.subject: A small pile of gold coins on a rough wooden table beside a tallow candle, the candle's light catching the metal, in a dim 1840s room.

storyboard.claim: Tom holds the truth of the murder as a valuable currency.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gold coins beside a candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the truth into a valuable thing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gold coins make the truth into currency that can be spent.

image.subject: A narrow limestone cave passage with dripping stone walls, a single candle flame held in a boy's hand casting small light, the walls closing in around him.

storyboard.claim: Spending the truth might cost Tom his life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A candle in a cave passage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the danger of using what he holds.
storyboard.addedInformation: The closing walls show the risk of acting.

image.subject: A crowded timber courtroom packed with townspeople on hard benches, a raised judge's bench at the front and a single window of light falling across the packed rows.

storyboard.claim: The courthouse is packed to the rafters for the trial.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A packed courtroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the reader into the courtroom for the trial.
storyboard.addedInformation: The packed benches show the town's appetite for spectacle.

storyboard.claim: The trial is the biggest entertainment in town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-item list of who attends.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds who is in the crowd.
storyboard.addedInformation: Both sexes and all ages attend, which shows the scale.

image.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard, pale and haggard, in a torn grey shirt with chains on his wrists, seated at the defendant's bench in a timber courtroom.

storyboard.claim: Potter sits pale and hopeless in chains before the court.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Muff seated in chains at the defendant's bench.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the accused man in the courtroom.
storyboard.addedInformation: His pale, hopeless face shows what the trial means to him.

image.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in his thirties in a torn, dirty brown coat and slouch hat sits still on a courtroom bench, a hard face with a scar, showing no emotion at all, eyes fixed forward.

storyboard.claim: Injun Joe sits completely calm in the courtroom.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Injun Joe seated, expressionless.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Places the killer in the same room as the accused.
storyboard.addedInformation: His calm stillness is the menace.

image.subject: A dignified man in his fifties in a black frock coat and white high collar, grey side-whiskers, taking his seat on a raised bench in a timber courtroom, a gavel on the bench before him.

storyboard.claim: The judge arrives to preside with grave order.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Judge Thatcher taking his seat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the authority of the court.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bench and gavel show the law taking its seat.

storyboard.claim: The prosecution lays out an ironclad case against Muff.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Place card for the courtroom, text only.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets out the case against the accused.
storyboard.addedInformation: The case is presented as airtight, which the town believes.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat with a neutral, thoughtful expression stands among a tense courtroom crowd, looking toward the defence table as a lawyer rises to speak.

storyboard.claim: Everyone assumes Muff is doomed until the defence speaks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grey-coated townsman in a tense courtroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the room's certainty before the turn.
storyboard.addedInformation: The crowd's expectant faces show the settled verdict.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet stands at the witness stand in a timber courtroom, breathless, his hand gripping the rail.

storyboard.claim: Tom is called to the stand and is breathless.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom at the witness stand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts Tom on the stand after the defence calls him.
storyboard.addedInformation: His gripping hand shows his fear.

left.label: TOM
left.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt standing at the witness stand, his mouth open, no words coming.

right.label: INJUN JOE
right.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in a torn brown coat and slouch hat, staring back coldly across the courtroom.

storyboard.claim: Tom stares at Injun Joe and his tongue fails him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom and Injun Joe facing each other across the room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the boy and killer face to face.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two faces show the stakes of the moment.

storyboard.claim: True heroism means risking your own capital, not other people's.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement.
storyboard.onScreenText: Risking your own capital, not someone else's.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the moment into the book's central idea.
storyboard.addedInformation: The contrast with trading chores and tickets is explicit.

storyboard.claim: True heroism requires risking your own physical safety.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Quotation card on plain background.
storyboard.onScreenText: "True heroism requires risking your own safety."
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the principle from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bar is set high on purpose.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt stands in a shaft of window light in a timber courtroom, one hand raised as he speaks, having stepped out from the crowd.

storyboard.claim: Tom steps out from behind his stagecraft to face real consequences.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom standing in window light, speaking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows Tom now standing in the open.
storyboard.addedInformation: The window light sets him apart from the crowd.

image.subject: A courtroom audience of townspeople in 1840s dress, faces turned intently toward a boy standing in the light, mouths slightly open, hanging on his every word.

storyboard.claim: Every eye is fixed on Tom as he warms to his subject.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Rapt courtroom faces turned toward Tom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the audience captured by Tom.
storyboard.addedInformation: Their faces show Tom has the room.

storyboard.claim: Tom weaves a spell and loses track of time, as he did with the boys.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement.
storyboard.onScreenText: Weaving a spell, taking no note of time.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Connects Tom's courtroom talk to his storytelling with the boys.
storyboard.addedInformation: The link to the earlier storytelling makes the point.

image.subject: An empty courtroom aisle with a toppled wooden bench and scattered papers on the floor, dust hanging in a shaft of light from a tall window, the room in disarray.

storyboard.claim: The climax erupts in the courtroom as the accused falls and the killer springs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A toppled bench in a courtroom aisle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the aftermath of the climax without violence.
storyboard.addedInformation: The disorder shows the chaos without depicting harm.

image.subject: An open courtroom window with a white curtain blowing inward, and beyond it a dark figure in a slouch hat running across a grassy yard away from the building.

storyboard.claim: The killer escapes through a window, and is gone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open window and a fleeing figure beyond.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the escape after the climax.
storyboard.addedInformation: The blowing curtain and running figure make the escape visible.

image.subject: The broad brown Mississippi at dusk, a steamboat's smoke on the horizon beyond a willow-lined shore, a raft tied to a willow in the foreground.

storyboard.claim: Tom breaks the community agreement and shatters the false story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The river at dusk with a steamboat on the horizon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the open river where the truth now flows.
storyboard.addedInformation: The river and steamboat suggest the story moving beyond the town.

storyboard.claim: If Tom risks his life to save an innocent man, is he finally a classic good boy?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Question card, text only.
storyboard.onScreenText: Is Tom finally the classic good boy?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the courtroom act into a judgment about Tom.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question sets up the Horatio Alger reading that follows.
